# ITGLA

> ITGLA means IT in a glance: a local-first desktop inventory connecting businesses, servers, services and domains for everyday management and handover preparation.

## Product

- ITGLA helps independent developers and small IT teams understand their resources and connections through business records, inventory tables, notes and a connection map.
- It supports tags, IP addresses, ports, spreadsheet imports, column mapping, custom fields, sorting, filtering, and copying individual cells.
- Current version: 0.6.1. The app supports manual service/domain inventory with versions, ports, tags, notes, hosting/origin servers, registrar/expiry/CDN fields, and directed service relations. Optional service account protection is Windows-only (CurrentUser DPAPI); Linux/macOS support metadata. Full database backups include this inventory; legacy project JSON does not.
- The desktop application stores its workspace in a local SQLite database.
- The desktop application does not require an account, provide cloud sync, upload workspaces, execute server commands, deploy services, or replace monitoring and secrets-management tools. Website sign-in is optional and separate from the local desktop application; signing in does not enable desktop cloud sync.

- macOS 14+ downloads are available separately for Apple silicon (arm64) and Intel (x86_64). Both packages are unsigned and not notarized.

## Product direction and current scope

- Brand idea: IT in a glance. Know what you have, how it connects, and what to pass on.
- Use existing records and notes to prepare context for staff changes, server moves, service handovers, company sales and technology transfers.
- Businesses currently support names, tags and notes. Notes can link to existing source repositories, deployment instructions and recovery documentation.
- Structured responsibility records, guided handover checklists, packaged handover reports, acceptance records and formal transfer workflows are planned; they are not current product features.
- ITGLA does not automatically transfer accounts, change permissions, migrate servers, establish asset ownership or complete legal/contractual transfers.

## Privacy boundary

Server inventory data belongs to the user and remains in the local desktop workspace. Website analytics are separate from desktop product data; see the privacy policy for website log and retention details.
